note: This skill encodes a data-extraction methodology, not jurisdiction-specific legal facts. Claims below are about the method and the interoperability/format standards it aligns to, plus the local script self-check. No live document set was extracted. The core discipline is anti-fabrication: an unreadable cell is a flagged blank, never a guessed value, and provenance is carried on every row.

claims.claim: A bulk extraction is only mergeable and computable when a fixed column schema, column order, and row grain are defined before extraction; extracting without a schema yields ragged output that will not stack across documents.
claims.raw_snippet: Every document produces rows with the SAME columns in the SAME order, including blanks for columns a given document lacks. This is what lets 200 documents stack into one table.

claims.claim: Every extracted row must carry its provenance (source document plus a page/row/cell location) so any value can be traced back and checked; a value without a source location is itself a flag.
claims.raw_snippet: Provenance columns: source_doc + a location (page / row / cell). A value without a source location cannot be checked, and an unverifiable extraction is exactly the fabrication risk this skill exists to prevent.

claims.claim: Extracted values normalize to unambiguous standards: dates to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), currency tags to ISO 4217 three-letter codes, and emitted CSV to RFC 4180 rules, so the output parses cleanly and is computable downstream.
claims.raw_snippet: ISO 8601 defines the unambiguous YYYY-MM-DD date format; ISO 4217 defines currency codes; RFC 4180 defines CSV quoting/header rules.

claims.claim: Ambiguous values (DD/MM vs MM/DD dates, US vs EU decimal/thousands separators, parenthesized/CR-DR signed numbers, split/merged cells) must be resolved from document context or flagged for review, never coerced with a single silent assumption; a misread separator is a 1000x error.
claims.raw_snippet: 1,234.50 (US) and 1.234,50 (EU) are the same amount written oppositely; misreading one is a 1000x error. 03/04/2024 = Mar 4 or Apr 3 -- resolve from context or flag.

claims.claim: The bundled table_extract.py is Python stdlib only (csv/json/re, no network, no third-party deps) and ships an embedded self-check runnable via --selftest, which passes; it normalizes US/EU money and disambiguable dates, flags ambiguous cells, and never guesses missing values.
claims.raw_snippet: `python scripts/table_extract.py --selftest` prints 'selftest OK'. Verified 2026-07-09 on python3.11. Normalizes 1,234.50->1234.5, 1.000,00->1000.0, (500)->-500; flags ambiguous 03/04 dates and non-numeric money cells. Does not reconcile totals, convert currencies, OCR images, or guess missing values.
